gaps.sentence: 'Get out of my way!' the guard snapped. The guard snapped at me ___ out of my way.
gaps.hint: snap at sb to do sth
gaps.explanation: The order is reported as snapped at me + to-infinitive.

gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'Have you ever been to Iceland?' she asked. She asked ___ ever been to Iceland.
gaps.explanation: Have you been → if I had been: if/whether with past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'It was me who ate the last biscuit,' the boy admitted. The boy ___ eating the last biscuit.
gaps.explanation: Admit takes a gerund (admit doing) or admit that + clause — never admit to do.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you speak Japanese?' the interviewer asked. The interviewer asked ___ Japanese.
gaps.explanation: Yes/no question → if I spoke; present simple backshifts to past simple.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw him this morning,' she said on Monday afternoon. She said she had seen him ___ morning.
gaps.explanation: This morning, reported later the same day, becomes that morning.

gaps.sentence: 'We stayed at this hotel last summer,' they recalled. They recalled that they had stayed at ___ hotel the summer before.
gaps.explanation: Demonstratives shift: this hotel → that hotel; last summer → the summer before.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
gaps.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.
